newsitem.title: USA: Carter-Wallace says board didn't act on bids.
newsitem.headline: Carter-Wallace says board didn't act on bids.

text.p: Carter-Wallace Inc Chairman Henry Hoyt told shareholders on Monday that the board took no independent action after two acquisition offers by investor Marvin Davis were rejected by the holding company CPI Development Corp.
"When CPI told the (Carter-Wallace) board it was not interested in Marvin Davis," the board decided it would be a "waste of corporate assets" to take any further action, Hoyt said.
CPI controls 82 percent of Carter-Wallace's voting power.

Hoyt's comments at the annual shareholder meeting at the Hotel DuPont, came in response to a shareholder's question about whether Davis' unsolicited proposals were ever analyzed by the Carter-Wallace board. Hoyt also confirmed that the
board hired no legal or financial advisors to evaluate Davis' $20 per share offer made earlier this year.
Hoyt refused to discuss unspecified "other current matters."
"Carter-Wallace does not reveal any information" on its strategies to avoid being put at a "serious competitive disadvantage," Hoyt said.

An analyst at the meeting told Reuters, "The market is just looking at Carter-Wallace's takeover value now. They have some great products which will be better utilized in the hands of a larger company.
"The question is can a company of this size and in the markets they are in support their brands, or does it make sense to combine Carter-Wallace with a larger company?" the analyst said.
Carter-Wallace makes pharmaceuticals, toiletries, personal care products, diagnostic specialties and pet products.
